subject: Literature
title: Aldous Huxley's Brave New World
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Aldous Huxley's Brave New World.

hook.text: Huxley warned that tyranny would not come through pain and punishment but through pleasure, comfort, and distraction.

buildup.text: In Brave New World, citizens are genetically engineered, drugged with soma, and kept happy by endless entertainment.

discovery.text: There is no dictator. People love their oppression because it feels like freedom, comfort, and constant pleasure.

twist.text: Many argue Huxley was more prescient than Orwell: our real threat is not tyranny but voluntary surrender to comfort.

climax.text: Brave New World asks the most disturbing question in dystopian fiction: what if people choose their own enslavement?

punchline.text: The scariest prison is the one you never want to leave.

quiz.question: How does Brave New World's dystopia differ from Orwell's 1984?
options: It controls people through pleasure and comfort rather than pain and punishment
It uses a single dictator rather than a political party
It is set in a rural society rather than a city
